title: A positive prime--zero feature intertwiner candidate and its pair-correlation gate
question: Can the actual xi divisor be intertwined with the von-Mangoldt dissipative law by a positive identity?

verdict.conclusion: A zero rho=1/2+eta+i gamma canonically defines a normalized von-Mangoldt feature vector psi_rho(n) proportional to sqrt(Lambda(n)) n^(-1-eta-i gamma).  Its squared diagonal is exactly p_eta and loses gamma.  A convergently weighted positive mixture of reflected diagonals equals the central p_0 ledger, or is even uniformly bounded relative to it along prime powers, if and only if every eta is zero.  This gives a sharp RH-equivalent positive intertwiner criterion.  Linear averaging of feature vectors does not create the diagonal.  The coherent quadratic lift has two-prime off-diagonal entries, but the Stage-41 logarithmic twirl removes those entries exactly and therefore needs no pair estimate for diagonal construction.  The dephased candidate is constructed, but the same-xi arithmetic frame bound is not proved.

globalMixtureCriterion.ordinateWeight: w_rho proportional to multiplicity/(gamma_rho^2+9/4), normalized over upper reflected pairs
globalMixtureCriterion.theorem: RH iff P_xi=p_0 on all prime powers; equivalently RH iff P_xi(n)/p_0(n) remains bounded along prime powers
globalMixtureCriterion.proof: under RH every eta is zero; if any eta>0 has positive weight, its p_-eta/p_0 term grows like n^(2eta) and makes the positive ratio unbounded

linearPhaseAverageNoGo.statement: translation-invariant averaging sends exp(i gamma u) to characteristic_mu(gamma) exp(i gamma u); a nonzero multiplier retains oscillation
linearPhaseAverageNoGo.consequence: a linear positive phase average cannot turn every unknown ordinate mode into the gamma-independent Gibbs diagonal

quadraticLift.diagonalBenefit: gamma cancels and p_eta is positive
quadraticLift.offDiagonalForm: sqrt(Lambda(n)Lambda(m)) n^(-1-eta) m^(-1-eta) exp[-i gamma log(n/m)]/M(2+2eta)
quadraticLift.gate: full coherent reconstruction is a two-prime correlation problem, but logarithmic dephasing removes every off-diagonal entry and needs no pair estimate for the positive diagonal

bridgeAttempts.attempt: linear positive averaging over log-scale translations
bridgeAttempts.reason: it multiplies each gamma Fourier mode by a characteristic function but retains its oscillatory sign unless the mode is annihilated

bridgeAttempts.attempt: annihilate every nonzero ordinate Fourier mode
bridgeAttempts.reason: it also deletes the zero information and cannot yield the eta-dependent positive mixture

bridgeAttempts.outcome: constructive but coherent off-diagonals contain prime pairs
bridgeAttempts.reason: its diagonal is p_eta and removes gamma, while its off-diagonal entries are two-prime correlations not fixed by the one-point Euler moment

bridgeAttempts.attempt: logarithmic conjugation twirl of the quadratic density
bridgeAttempts.reason: sinc(T log(n/m)) tends to zero for n!=m and leaves p_eta exactly, so no pair estimate is needed for the dephased map
positivity over the full admissible autocorrelation class is the Weil criterion
it supplies the required quadratic prime-pair control only at the unresolved square-root boundary

nextNarrowTarget.statement: prove from fixed prime arithmetic a positive frame or diagonal identity P_xi=p_0 for the dephased ordinate-weighted von-Mangoldt features
nextNarrowTarget.weakerSufficientForm: a uniform bound P_xi(n)<=C p_0(n) along all prime powers already excludes every eta>0
nextNarrowTarget.failFast: logarithmic twirling resolves phase removal; any claimed prime-side proof must establish the RH-equivalent global bound rather than assume Weil positivity, critical energy or another equivalent condition

finiteComputation.scope: feature normalization, mixture separation, phase-average signs and pair-kernel samples are deterministic truncated checks; the rigidity theorem is analytic
